title: Claude Opus 5.5 fast mode 结束研究预览并移除等待名单
content:
ClaudeDevs· @ClaudeDevs · X·· 1 小时前精选AI 评分66
AI 导读
Anthropic 宣布 Claude 平台上的 Opus 5.5 fast mode 不再处于研究预览阶段，并已移除等待名单。该模式速度最高提升 2.5 倍，定价为 $8 / $40 per million tokens；现已登陆 Microsoft Foundry（Azure 托管），Google Cloud 即将支持。Claude Code 中的 fast mode 保持不变，消耗额外 usage credits。文档见 https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/fast-mode
推荐理由
原文给出了 fast mode 正式开放后的速度、定价和平台覆盖变化，读者可据此评估是否切换到该模式。
正文 · AI 翻译
Claude 平台中的 Opus 5.5 快速模式已不再处于研究预览阶段，我们已取消等候名单！
它仍是同一个 Opus 5.5，但速度最高提升 2.5 倍，价格为每百万 token $8 / $40。
它也可在 Microsoft Foundry（托管于 Azure）中使用，Google Cloud 即将推出。
Claude Code 中的快速模式保持不变，并使用额外用量额度。
在此查看我们的文档：
https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/fast-mode

report.summary: Anthropic's Opus 5.5 fast mode exits research preview and drops its waitlist, offering up to 2.5x speed at $8/$40 per million tokens across Claude platforms and Microsoft Foundry.
report.background: Anthropic first positioned Opus 5.5 fast mode as a research preview, using a waitlist to manage capacity while gathering latency and reliability data. The move reflects broader industry demand for low-latency inference, especially for agentic coding, real-time assistants, and enterprise automation, where response time affects user experience and workflow throughput. Model providers increasingly separate intelligence from serving speed, offering premium fast tiers as a way to monetize latency-sensitive workloads without releasing a new model. Anthropic's expansion to Microsoft Foundry and planned Google Cloud support also shows multi-cloud distribution is becoming central to enterprise AI procurement, as customers want models available inside existing cloud, security, and billing environments. Removing the waitlist signals that capacity and demand planning now support general availability.
key_points: Opus 5.5 fast mode is now generally available: Anthropic has ended its research preview and removed the waitlist. It remains the same Opus 5.5 model, but is optimized to run up to 2.5x faster. That makes it relevant for interactive coding, real-time agents, customer support, and other workflows where latency is a primary constraint.

Pricing is $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. This is a premium speed tier, not a discount. Teams should compare total cost against standard Opus 5.5, because faster responses may justify higher spend only when latency directly improves conversion, retention, or developer productivity.

Availability expands beyond the Claude platform: fast mode is live on Microsoft Foundry, hosted on Azure, with Google Cloud support coming soon. Enterprise buyers can use their preferred cloud contracts, identity, and security controls. Claude Code fast mode remains unchanged and consumes extra usage credits, so coding users should watch quota and billing.

Anthropic published official docs at platform.claude.com. Developers can now test fast mode in production-like workloads without waitlist friction. The key decision is workload routing: use fast mode for latency-critical calls and standard mode for batch, background, or cost-sensitive tasks to balance speed and spend.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Anthropic's move normalizes premium low-latency inference as a product tier. Competitors such as OpenAI, Google, and open-model providers may face pressure to offer comparable fast modes or clear latency guarantees. For developers, it simplifies access to high-speed Opus 5.5 and enables more responsive agents, but increases cost-optimization work: teams need token budgets, routing logic, and observability to avoid surprise bills. Claude Code users must manage extra usage credits. For regular users, faster Claude-powered apps and coding assistants should feel snappier, though the premium pricing may be passed on by commercial products. The waitlist removal also signals capacity confidence, which matters for production adoption.
report.tools: Follow Anthropic's official fast-mode docs and Microsoft Foundry/Azure AI documentation. For multi-provider routing and cost control, evaluate LiteLLM, OpenRouter, or Portkey. Use observability tools like Langfuse, Helicone, or Weights & Biases Weave to track latency and token spend. Claude Code users should monitor usage credits. For agent frameworks, LangChain, LlamaIndex, and OpenAI Agents SDK can help compare fast versus standard routing.
